1 ” to allow audio playback CHILD ABUSE IN THE COMMUNITY. [Music] Hallo learner, welcome to a social studies lesson for grade 4. Today we shall learn about child abuse in the community. Your radio teacher is Eugene Kimani. Welcome to the program. [Music]

2 ” to allow audio playback Hallo learner, welcome to our social studies grade 4 lesson. Today, we shall learn about ways in which children are abused in the community. So get your book and pencil and let us learn social studies. I am your radio teacher Eugene kimani [Music] I hope you have the book and pen ready and set to learn. We are going to start the lesson by remembering what we learnt about qualities of a good learner. What did we say are the good qualities of a learner in school? Answer when you hear the music. [Music] Very good, we said that good qualities of a learner include: being kind to others; being honest; caring for others; being obedient; being responsible; being hardworking; being humble; Being tolerant. Today we are going to learn about forms of child abuse in the community. Now what is child abuse? Answer when you hear the music [Music] Very good, child abuse is the crime of harming a child in a physical, sexual or emotional way. Now let us look at the ways in which children are abused in the community. Write down three ways you know in which children are harmed or treated badly in the community. Do that when you hear the music. [Music] Very good, I know you have answers like: slavery, child labour, child trafficking, harming or mistreating children with special needs sexual abuse, early and forced marriages, and female circumcision. Now, we are going to talk about these abuses. [Music] Very good, let us start with child labour. What is child labour? Child labour is when children are forced to work for money instead of going to school. For example: being sent to work in a quarry for money to help your parents or guardian to buy food instead of going to school. Example two: A girl sent to work as a house help to earn money to assist parents or guardian at home. Now let us look at slavery as a form of child abuse. What is slavery? Answer when you hear the music [Music] Very good, child slavery is when some children are sold to people who make them do hard work without pay. For example: when a parent is paid to let his or her child to go and work in a farm and the child is not paid. Now let us look at sexual abuse. What is sexual abuse? Answer when you hear the music [Music] I hope you have answered. Sexual abuse is when young children below the age of 18 years are forced to engage in sexual acts with adults. For example: when a young girl below the age of 18 years is forced to get married to an adult. Example two: When a young child is raped or forced to engage in sexual acts with an adult.

3 ” to allow audio playback Now let us look at child trafficking. What is child trafficking? Answer when you hear the music [Music] Very good, child trafficking is when children are stolen or sold in other countries or other parts of the country. For example: a child may be stolen from Nairobi and sold in Mombasa. Second example : A child can also be stolen from Tanzania and sold in Kenya. Now let us look at abuse of children with special needs. How can children with special needs be abused? [Music] Very good, children with special needs can also be abused in many ways like: When they are not allowed to move around but stay in one place. When they are not allowed to play with other children. When they are hidden and locked up in their houses with their parents or guardian. Now talk with your parent or guardian how you will know that a child has been abused? That is the end of our lesson for today. [Music] You have been listening to a social studies programme for grade 4 learners. Your radio teacher was Eugene Kimani. This programme was recorded by John Mbiti. It was produced by Zachary Kago for Educational Media Directorate, Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development. Until next time. Goodbye. [Music]
